body.text: Overview and Empirical Foundations of Economy of East Africa

Most operators overlook how Economy of East Africa drives unit economics and competitive moats at scale. Understanding its real-world mechanics reveals why disciplined organizations outperform during market shifts.

The economy of East Africa is a diverse and rapidly developing regional economy, with agriculture playing a pivotal role as a backbone of the economy. 935 trillion (PPP) accounting for approximately 18% of Africa's total GDP. Kenya and Ethiopia are the largest national economies, together contributing roughly 48% of the regional economy. Nairobi and Addis Ababa are the main economic hubs, while other major economic centres include Dar es Salaam, Kampala, Mombasa, and Kigali.

As of 2026, East Africa’s economies varied significantly in size and wealth with the region having both the most wealthiest countries and most poorest countries in Africa. Kenya was the largest state economy, with a GDP of $151 billion, followed by Ethiopia at $127 billion and Tanzania at $96 billion. 37 billion) had the smallest economies.
